correctness.rationale: Exact conserved logarithmic leaf ratios select a unique positive equilibrium. Proper Volterra entropy gives derivative -d(u-U)^2, trapping all positive trajectories and enabling LaSalle convergence to that point. The leaf-restricted Jacobian polynomial lambda²+Ud lambda+UB follows from exact coordinates; strict convex weighted response range gives necessary and sufficient coexistence. In the focus regime, linear canonical coordinates give angular speed tending to omega=sqrt(UB-U²d²/4); level intersections occur twice per rotation, hence omega/pi crossings per time. In the distinct node regime, asymptotic eigenvector direction (including on the strong-stable curve) makes the central displacement eventually single-signed. The m=2 divider is algebraically exact. A symbolic checker validates the dissipation, conserved ratio and full Jacobian for the concrete three-species case; finite integrations corroborate but do not prove the asymptotic statements. Repeated root deliberately excluded.

value.rationale: Graph structure and global attraction do not decide which approach mode is selected by a particular positive initial composition. In a natural ecological star with an equilibrium continuum, the precise iff condition for coexistence of damped oscillatory and nonoscillatory transients at unchanged coefficients is a meaningful phase-portrait boundary. The explicit conserved initial-ratio divider and asymptotic crossings per time turn the qualitative distinction into computable, observable quantities. This structural classification works for all finite numbers of leaves, not a selected parameter sample.
